# Unit G, phase 1: the new text's assertions, one per sentence

#### The commit, in full
- V1 The committed solution is applied as an `init!` in every respect.
- V2 It is `override(baseline, condition(d))` through boundary zero, with the pre-write root-input totality check (§14.6), the sequence (§14.5) and guards at commit. [§14.6, §14.5]
- V3 That check requires the application to cover every root input.
- V4 The `t0` argument that anchors the grid, and its default, are the same for both init-service entry points (§14.5, D-110). [§14.5, D-110]
- V5 The recorders (the trace and the log jointly) restart exactly as §12.6 states for `init!` (D-110). [§12.6, D-110]
- V6 The trace (the primary record of a session) and the log are new objects.
- V7 Any batches still in staging cells (where a device's pending write batch waits between drains) are cleared.
- V8 A fresh recording that starts at its own anchor is the natural shape of unattended mode.
- V9 Trim is not offered at a point reached by flying.
- V10 It takes an authored baseline.
- V11 Fly-then-retrim is spelled as a `checkpoint` of the flight, then a trim baseline authored from what the checkpoint (the `Model`'s state at a frame top as one value) shows (D-273). [D-273]

#### The report
- V12 `trim!` returns a structured `TrimReport` (D-070). [D-070]
- V13 The sketch names its eleven fields in order.
- V14 [code block] # what trim! returns: a value to read, never an exception to catch
- V15 The list below takes the fields in turn.
- V16 `converged` is the service's own box test at the returned point, never a backend's opinion.
- V17 `solution` is the solution NamedTuple.
- V18 It is guess-shaped, hence warm-startable.
- V19 `residuals` are the solved-point residuals, and `tolerances` the tolerances they come with (§14.5, D-155). [§14.5, D-155]

- V21 `committed_residuals` are the committed-state residuals, the same residuals re-gathered from the boundary-zero world after the commit.
- V22 `committed_checks` holds the committed-state checks, the check function's return at the committed state.
- V23 They are gathered beside the committed-state residuals and empty when the problem declares none (§14.7). [§14.7]
- V24 `status` is the backend's returned status, and `n_evaluations` and `n_iterations` are its evaluation and iteration counts.
- V25 These are diagnostic throughout, informative about how the solve went and decisive about nothing.
- V26 `saturated` is the saturated-bounds list.
- V27 `fired_events` holds the commit's fired events, as component paths and event names.

- V29 The committed-state residuals are nearly free (D-155). [D-155]
- V30 Boundary zero's sweep has already run, so the residuals' declared reads need one derivative evaluation and a gather from it.
- V31 There is no offset caveat to carry.
- V32 Every output stage publishes at boundary zero (D-205, §14.5). [D-205, §14.5]
- V33 A residual reading the port (one declared name, one cell) of an offset component therefore reads a commit-refreshed cell like any other.
- V34 Those committed-state residuals are the numbers describing the state the simulation is actually in, which is the point a `linearize` at its default operating point reads.

#### The AD obligation
- V76 The default formulation requires `Dual` genericity of exactly the continuous output-stage chains and `x_deriv`, plus the user's assignment and residual math (D-070). [D-070] (bold)
- V77 The discrete tier's stages and `s_update`, and the event system's guards and handlers, never see a `Dual`.
- V78 They are frozen constants with zero partials, semantically exact (§8.2). [§8.2]
- V79 This is not a new obligation.
- V80 It is the same activation linearization is defined on.
- V81 AD-readiness is also a build-checked property.
- V82 A pinned intermediate (a value held at `Float64` inside authored continuous math) makes the Dual probe fail with a culprit-naming `MethodError` or `InexactError` (D-307). [D-307]
- V83 `build(world; activations)` puts the probe in CI (D-280). [D-280]
- V84 The robustness comes from enforcement, not hope.
- V85 An audit of Flight.jl's Cessna 172 model (`c172.jl`) against this obligation took one afternoon (D-070). [D-070]
- V86 Its findings on tables and saturations follow, and its two Flight.jl-only findings, on the landing gear and the `norm`-at-zero guards, are in the `migration_outline.md` companion.
- V87 `Interpolations.jl` tables (propeller coefficient maps, engine maps) must accept generic scalars.
- V88 They do.
- V89 A call `itp(x::Dual)` works through the `BSpline`/`scale`/`extrapolate` compositions in Flight.jl's tables.
- V90 Prefer cubic knots over linear where partials matter, though, since linear knots make Jacobian entries piecewise-constant.
- V91 That is no regression against finite differences (D-307). [D-307]
- V92 A manual chain rule via `Interpolations.gradient` is the escape hatch for anything exotic, and the pattern for wrapping non-Julia black boxes (§14.10, D-266). [§14.10, D-266]
- V93 In-model saturations (actuator limits, idle/FRC clamps) zero Jacobian columns when active.
- V94 LM damping tolerates the rank deficiency, and the report names the saturated variable (D-070). [D-070]
- V95 Cruise trim leaves those saturations inactive.
- V96 The derivative-free fallback would be chosen per call, through the one `backend =` keyword.

### 14.9 Mounting: problems as relocatable values
- V97 This section treats a `TrimProblem` (the closed nine-field value a trim solves) as a relocatable value.
- V98 Mounting (relocating a whole problem or tap set to a prefix) is the work of `at`, the scoping combinator.
- V99 The section says what a problem is, then how `at` lifts one, how a mounted read set and mounted input entries resolve, why a problem never authors the environment, and how worlds, thin rigs and swarms use the lift.
- V100 A `TrimProblem` is not a condition but an implicitly specified condition (D-071). [D-071] (bold)
- V101 A condition is the datum that says "set this build to this state".
- V102 `condition` is a condition-valued function over the decision space.
- V103 `reads`/`residuals` are the equations that pin the free variables down.
- V104 `guess`, `lower` and `upper` say where to search.
- V105 Solving makes the implicit condition explicit.
- V106 The commit is then literally an init, `override(baseline, condition(d))` through boundary zero (the initialization boundary, the ordinary macro-sequence with an empty integrate).
- V107 The services unify as clients of one condition algebra.
- V108 `init!` applies an explicit condition, and `trim!` searches a family for the member satisfying its equations.
- V109 `at` lifts a problem field by field, and each field falls in one of three cases (D-071, D-277). [D-071, D-277] (bold)
- V110 The `condition` field is condition-producing (path-relative), so the lift post-composes it.
- V111 The `reads` field is a read set, and the lift prepends the prefix to the set's mount chain (the prefixes it is mounted under, root first).
- V112 Every other field is path-free and passes through.
- V113 The rule that residual math sees only the gathered NamedTuple (§14.7) is what makes the residuals path-free. [§14.7]
- V114 [code block] at(prefix::String, p::TrimProblem) = TrimProblem(
- V115 The condition side needs nothing new at resolution.
- V116 The flattening accumulator of §14.3 enters each `Scoped` wrapper and prefixes every condition entry below it. [§14.3]
- V117 A read set carries its mount chain as data (D-277). [D-277] (bold)
- V118 `at(prefix, read_set)` prepends the prefix to that chain and joins nothing.
- V119 A `Reads` value is no condition node, so `Scoped` never wraps one.
- V120 Resolution walks the chain from the root, each prefix from the level the previous one reached (§13.3, D-277). [§13.3, D-277] (bold)
- V121 It then rebases every selector (one of the closed family of deferred reads) to the root before the selector resolves.
- V122 A path selector's path is joined to the mount (`"vehicle/dynamics"` → `"wing/vehicle/dynamics"`).
- V123 `get_input` names an input face (the name a port wears on its component's boundary) of the mount level.
- V124 It follows the export chain to the root input it lands on (the root component's own input face).
- V125 `get_face` names an output face of the mount level and reads its producer's port (D-277). [D-277]
- V126 A refusal spells the selector as authored and names the mount (D-277). [D-277] (bold)
- V127 `at` refuses an empty prefix on a read set, as it does on a condition node (§14.2), and raises `ReadSetMisuse`. [§14.2]
- V128 A problem's lift and a tap set's lift reach that refusal through `at` on their read sets (D-278). [D-278]
- V129 Input entries authored in the aircraft's face vocabulary resolve through the export chain from the mount point (D-071). [D-071] (bold)
- V130 Mounted at `"wing"`, the input entry `throttle` resolves to root input `"wing.throttle"`.
- V131 An unexported face fails resolution by name, and correctly so (§14.2). [§14.2]
- V132 An internally wired input (a scenario component driving the wingman's throttle) is untrimmable from outside.
- V133 Resolution refuses it by name, with the producer that drives it in hand, as `ConditionResolution` for a condition entry and as `ReadResolution` for a `get_input`.
- V134 The service compiles the scoped condition and reads, and runs the identical loop.
- V135 It never knows where its paths are mounted.
- V136 A problem never authors the environment (D-139). [D-139] (bold)
- V137 The environment is the business of the world and of the `baseline` (the full-coverage condition `trim!` takes as a keyword).
- V138 In a full world it is a sibling component's root inputs.
- V139 In a thin rig it is a root input holding an isbits handle (an immutable query object carried on an ordinary port).
- V140 It can also be a constant source (a library component publishing a value its instance holds) holding a bulk-data handle (D-364). [D-364]
- V141 The problem receives its handles through the user parameter record (§14.7), and only queries them. [§14.7]
- V142 The reason is the resolution rule stated above.
- V143 A condition entry naming an internally wired input fails by name, correctly.
- V144 A problem writing an environment face would therefore be applicable only to those rigs where that face happens to be unconnected.
- V145 The relocatability this section exists to guarantee would be lost.
- V146 The world wrapper dissolves (D-071). [D-071] (bold)
- V147 Flight.jl's `f_init!(::Model{<:SimpleWorld})` (initialize environment, then call the aircraft's trim) has no successor method.
- V148 The environment, the other aircraft and all root inputs are covered by the `baseline` condition (§14.6), applied once at setup. [§14.6]
- V149 The commit is `override(baseline, at(mount, condition(d)))`.
- V150 Method nesting became value layering.
- V151 "Aircraft as root" is a thin world.
- V152 Design tasks use a shipped rig, `design_world(ac)` (D-071). [D-071] (bold)
- V153 They need one because by default the aircraft is not literally the root.
- V154 Its environment inputs are function-valued signals (§4.4), wired from provider components. [§4.4]
- V155 The rig is `design_world(ac)` = aircraft + `SimpleAtmosphere(wind = NoWind())` + `HorizontalTerrain`, where `SimpleAtmosphere` and `NoWind` are Flight.jl's atmosphere types.
- V156 `design_world` promotes the ad-hoc atmosphere and terrain `Model`s inside Flight.jl's `linearize` to a named artifact.
- V157 There is one mechanism.
- V158 The "root" case is the shallowest world, and the trim problem mounts at `"aircraft"` like anywhere else.
- V159 Leaving an environment face unconnected is legal by construction, though, for an isbits handle.
- V160 The face becomes an ordinary root input holding the handle value, written by the `baseline` like any other root input.
- V161 That is the test-rig idiom.
- V162 It is the function-valued sibling of a constant source, with zero ceremony for a frozen environment.
- V163 A handle that references bulk data is never a root input, and the rig wires a constant source holding it (D-364). [D-364] (bold)
- V164 §4.4 states why such a handle cannot be a root input (D-237). [§4.4, D-237]
- V165 For design tasks the shipped rig stays `design_world(ac)`.
- V166 That keeps the environment's tunables in the root-input vocabulary that conditions, linearization's input surface and the trace header (the trace's fixed preamble) already speak.
- V167 The swarm doctrine covers trims of several aircraft.
- V168 The service solves one problem at a time (D-071). [D-071] (bold)
- V169 Sequential independent trims (trim lead, commit, trim wing against the committed world) cover weak or one-way coupling.
- V170 A joint trim is user-side value composition.
- V171 Concatenate decision NamedTuples under prefixed names, combine the scoped condition trees, and stack the residuals.
- V172 If joint trims become routine, a `product(p₁ => "lead", p₂ => "wing")` helper is the extension recorded for them (D-071). [D-071] (bold)
- V173 That helper is recorded, not built (a worked-out extension deliberately left unimplemented, its seams named).
